text:
Maya: FYI noticed p99 jump on prod around 11:02. Root traces point at the continuous-batcher queue — long wait before microbatch dispatch.

Kevin: Can you paste the perf graphs? p95/p99 numbers and any recent config changes?

PerfBot: auto-report: 
- window=10m, model=rwd-ggml-16k
- p50=40ms p95=220ms p99=820ms (baseline yesterday p99 ~420ms)
- avg queue_delay_ms increased from 8 -> 120ms
- max_wait_ms spikes correlate with CPU steal on host pool-03
(reports: https://perf.internal/reports/171560) :robot_face:

Sasha: I pulled the scheduler logs. We pushed a tweak two hours before regressions: 
```yaml
scheduler:
  continuous_batching:
    max_batch_tokens: 4096  # was 8192 previously for throughput
    max_wait_ms: 50        # was 20 before the experiment
    microbatch_target: 8   # target requests per microbatch
```
That change was intended to reduce memory pressure but may be enlarging queue blocks.

Olivia: Quick notes from profiling (local repro):
- Kernel selection flips to fused_attention for seq_len >= 512; fused path has better throughput but higher cold-start latency on small microbatches.
- KV cache behavior: when multiple concurrent streams hit large KV footprint, we see cache eviction thrashing -> extra device copies and occasional rewarm that shows as tail spikes.
- Sample profile excerpt: 
```
Timeline (ms): queue=110, dispatch=5, compute=280, kv_fetch=45, postproc=6
Kernel selected: fused_attention_v2 (seq=1024)
KV cache hit=0.86
```

Olivia: Hypothesis: increasing max_wait_ms to 50 allowed bigger aggregate microbatches which hit fused kernels often — good for throughput but if a microbatch contains some long-seq requests (>=1k) it stalls others in queue causing p99 blowup. Also KV cache churn exacerbates tail latency.

Ryan: Agreed. We saw a previous regression when we switched default kernel selector to prefer fused_attention for seq >= 512. Rollback reduced p99 by ~300ms in canary.

Maya: Can we run a short A/B: pool-A uses conservative scheduler (max_batch_tokens=2048, max_wait_ms=12), pool-B retains current (4096/50) and route 10% traffic to pool-B. Need p50/p95/p99 + throughput over 30m.

Kevin: Also instrument microbatch size distribution and per-request seq_len sampling so we can correlate long seqs to queue delays. Add a histogram metric microbatch_size and seq_len_percentiles.

PerfBot: scheduled experiment created: exp_id=cb-2024-03-12-17. Metrics to collect: request.latency.{p50,p95,p99}, serving.throughput, microbatch.size.hist, kv.cache.hit_rate, kernel.selector.counts.

Sasha: Quick config patch I propose for pool-A: 
```yaml
continuous_batching:
  max_batch_tokens: 2048
  max_wait_ms: 12
  pref_fused_threshold: 768  # keep fused kernels for very long seqs only
  kv_cache_mode: conservative  # avoid aggressive prefetch/eviction
```
I'll push to staging and run local load test.

Olivia: Load-test snapshot (staging, 50k requests, mixed seq distribution):
- config A (2048/12): throughput=72 req/s, p95=180ms, p99=360ms
- config B (4096/50): throughput=95 req/s, p95=150ms, p99=740ms
Tradeoff clear: B increases throughput but doubles p99.

Kevin: Can we tune microbatch_target to bias toward smaller microbatches under high tail risk? e.g., microbatch_target=4 during detected p99 surge.

Maya: Good idea. Add an autoscaler rule: if p99 > 500ms for 2 minutes, switch to safe config (A). Also add gradual ramp back.

Ryan: On the kernel side we can add a per-microbatch cost estimator: estimate compute time based on seq_len distribution in the batch and select kernel that minimizes tail impact (not just aggregate throughput). Might need tiny offline ML to predict tail-safety.

Olivia: I'll prototype heuristic: pick fused only if median_seq_len > threshold AND kv_cache_hit_rate > 0.9. Otherwise prefer low-latency kernel.

PerfBot: profiling delta after staging push (10m window): 
- microbatch_size median down 2 -> better interleaving
- p99 reduced from 740ms -> 380ms on pool-A
- throughput loss ~25% on pool-A vs pool-B
(details: https://perf.internal/diffs/cb-2024-03-12)

Sasha: Rolling change to canary tomorrow 09:30PT. Owners: Sasha (deploy), Olivia (profiler/heuristics), Ryan (kernel selector patch), Kevin (monitoring + autoscaler rule), Maya (incident owner).

Maya: Thanks. Capture action items in PR and link experiment id. We'll review after 1h of canary traffic. :white_check_mark:

Kevin: One more: add logging for queue composition when queue_delay > 100ms: dump first 5 seq_lens and kernel choices so we can see offending patterns without heavy traces.

Ryan: Will add that. Keeps trace sampling light.

PerfBot: note: next scheduled perf-summary will post to #eng-runtime in 35m.

Maya: Closing thread — re-open if p99 spikes during canary.
